name: Nashville
lede: Music City's disc golf is friendly, woodsy, and busier than the stats suggest — Seven Oaks is one of the South's great community courses. We're publishing the metro's best first.
introParagraphs: Nashville disc golf revolves around Seven Oaks — the impeccably maintained 21-hole course that's been the city's beating heart since 1989, with a bonus three-hole loop the locals treat as a warm-down. Cedar Hill in Madison adds another 21 holes with a 3-hole inner loop and varied terrain, and Crockett Park in Brentwood is the gentle rolling-hills option.
All three of our published Nashville courses are free, and the community is famously welcoming — expect to leave with new friends and a few new disc golf plans.
New here? Seven Oaks first — it's the course everyone means when they talk about Nashville disc golf.

faqs.question: How many disc golf courses are in the Nashville metro?
faqs.answer: Around 25 courses across the metro. We're publishing the best first — 3 are live today, with more added every week.

faqs.question: What's the best disc golf course in Nashville?
faqs.answer: Seven Oaks — the exquisitely maintained 21-hole course that anchors the city's scene. Cedar Hill in Madison is the varied-terrain runner-up.

faqs.question: Are Nashville's disc golf courses free?
faqs.answer: Yes — all three of our published courses (Seven Oaks, Cedar Hill, Crockett) are free to play.

faqs.question: What's the best beginner course in Nashville?
faqs.answer: Crockett Park in Brentwood — gentle rolling hills and a friendly layout. Seven Oaks is also welcoming despite being the local favorite.
